oracle: compress the input's bytes with the JSONL backend's compressZstdFrame, Node's asynchronous zstdCompress with ZSTD_c_checksumFlag set; list the frame's hex when it is at most 512 bytes, otherwise its length and SHA-256
history: Version 1: 13 cases. The frames Rust's Zstd writer compresses equal the TypeScript backend's byte for byte: the libzstd 1.5.7 that Node 22.19.0, 24.21.0, and 26.10.0 bundle and zstd-sys 2.1.0+zstd.1.5.7 at the default level 3, the frame streamed with ZSTD_e_continue and ended by an empty ZSTD_e_end, as Node's zlib stream does, so the header has no content size, a window descriptor of 2 MiB, and a checksum. An input is text, a string repeated, rows of turn/start events numbered from 0, or bytes of the xorshift32 generator (x ^= x << 13; x ^= x >>> 17; x ^= x << 5, each byte the low 8 bits) from a seed; the cases cover an empty input, Node's 16 KiB output chunk, the 128 KiB block, raw incompressible blocks, and inputs past the 2 MiB window. The table names that libzstd version, and both arms refuse to compare on any other, so a Node or zstd-sys upgrade reports the version rather than a hex difference. Every expectation was recorded from the TypeScript backend's compressZstdFrame before the Rust arm ran. Compressing the same inputs with ZSTD_e_end in one call, which records the content size, failed every case.
